# 

# Objective/Goal 

* Give Shopify Merchants using Quickbooks Online the ability to easily process payment transactions from Shopify as Invoices in Quickbooks Online  
    
* Ideally the app would run once a day and capture any payments made since the last time the query was executed  
    
* Eliminate the need to double book transactions between shopify and Quickbooks

#  Success metrics

List the project goals and the metrics you’ll be using to determine the project’s success.

| Goal | Metric |
| :---- | :---- |
| \# of orders processed via connector | E.g. 254 Orders processed in June (or 2019, etc) |
| \# of invoices processed / week | E.g. 254 Invoices processed in May |
| \# of pdf reports generated  | E.g. 254 pdf reports generated |

# Features

|  | Requirement | User story | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Shopify Payments & Transactions | Ability to extract Orders (or Transactions) that are included in a Shopify Payout  | Goal is to use data from the Payments API in orderowrder to find the Payouts and Transactions  [https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify\_payments](https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify_payments) The payouts endpoint contains high-level information (e.g. total amount) [https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify\_payments/payout](https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify_payments/payout) The Transactions endpoint should provide the detail for each payout [https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify\_payments/transaction](https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/shopify_payments/transaction) For example, if the Payout Amount is $100, then using the payout date or amount, we should be able to find the Orders.  Continuing this example, there could be 2 or more orders, whose aggregate sum should equal the payout amount. (if it doesn’t then something is wrong 😁)  |
| 2 | Shopify Orders | Ability to use the Order ids from the Payments API to query the Transaction API  | For each payout, find the Transactions that were included The identifiers found from this query will be needed to make a 2nd query Using the list of Identifiers found in the Payouts query, loop through each Identifier to get the details for each order (in the Payout) which will include Order fields such as: Transaction Type \= Charge id email created\_at number note token gateway test total\_price subtotal\_price total\_tax taxes\_included currency total\_discounts total\_line\_items\_price name total\_price\_usd order\_number tax\_lines Created\_at Number Token Test total\_price subtotal\_price  |
| 3 | Payout Detail | Ability to view items that were processed through the connector in | The goal of this feature is to capture new Payouts Added to the Payouts API The app should monitor for Payouts with the Status “Paid”  Generally speaking, the Payout Date should be Today’s Date Ideally, the transactional data should not be stored but if required, capture the data, for each merchant, in the Shopify endpoint at runtime See example below (scroll to the sub heading marked Payout Detail and look for the column in the image is labeled “Reference”)  Using the Payout, compare the Charges, Refunds, Adjustments, Fees, and Total to the Payout Detail (Transaction Query) The sum of each field the Orders query should \= the amount of the Payout Each order/transaction in a Payout will be used to create the invoice in Quickbooks   |
| 4 | Invoicing | Ability to create a Quickbooks invoice | Goal of this feature is to create an invoice in Quickbooks for each Transaction in a Payout [https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/develop/tutorials/create-an-invoice\#invoice-intro](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/develop/tutorials/create-an-invoice#invoice-intro) These fields (at a minimum) should be captured from Shopify to POST into Quickbooks (from [https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/orders/order\#show-2019-10)](https://help.shopify.com/en/api/reference/orders/order#show-2019-10\))  |
| 5 | Order Link | Ability to view the Shopify URL on a Quickbooks Invoice | One of the goals of this app is to eliminate the need to double book entries between Shopify and Quickbooks Users should be able view the URL that contains a link to the order so that the Quickbooks transactions can be audited easily. For example, if a Quickbooks user is viewing an invoice, they may want to validate the details of the transaction Providing a link can make it easy for these users to validate the accounting entries in Quickbooks to the data processed by Shopify Ideally, this is a link to a pdf version of the transaction, but if not, the URL to the order in shopify admin would suffice  |
| 6 | Shopify Tags | Ability to update Shopify Order Tags when Payouts are processed by Quickbooks | After the payout is made to the bank, and the transactions are processed through the workflow, a Shopify Tag should be added to let Shopify Admin users know that those items were “Booked”  |
| 7 | Metrics | Ability for admin user to view the success metrics | Admin users should be able to view these stats: \# of orders processed via connector \# of invoices processed / week \# of pdf reports generated   |
| 8 | Tests | Ability to test the app for stability | There should be automated tests for these features Shopify Connection Shopify Orders API Shopify Transactions API Quickbooks Connection Quickbooks Invoice The \# of Payouts Queried The \# of Transactions Processed by the Connector each day and historically The \# of Invoices Created in Quickbooks The \# of Orders Queried  |

# 

# Acceptance Tests

These tests will be used to perform functional testing of the app

Given: Shopify Admin User is viewing their dashboard and noticed there was a payout yesterday in the amount of $2.000. The payout contained 3 transactions, for invoice ids \#101, \#102, \#103  
The user should expect to be able to: 

* Open quickbooks and see 3 invoices with id, \#101, \#102, \#103  
* See each invoice in Quickbooks contains  
  * Shopify ID   
  * Total amount  
  * Total Tax  
  * Discount  
  * Shipping  
  * Link to the Order (as a pdf or URL) in Shopify  
* Open the Shopify Admin Payouts Screen and see   
  * A “Booked” tag for any payout that was processed through Quickbooks
